title: Assessing the condition of production and rewilded ecosystems: The Red List of Ecosystems can help
content:
The Red List of Ecosystems, a globally accepted framework to assess the condition of ecosystems, has been primarily developed with natural ecosystems in mind. We argue that this framework is also suitable for assessing production and rewilded ecosystems, while underlining its flexibility, which enables it to keep pace with recent conceptual and technological developments in biodiversity monitoring and ecosystem science.


Abstract

The Red List of Ecosystems (RLE), a globally accepted framework to assess the condition of ecosystems, is key to the implementation of an ecosystem-based approach to environmental management. However, the RLE has been primarily developed with natural ecosystems in mind, with little discussion to date on its suitability for assessing production or rewilded ecosystems or its potential for integrating new data types. Here, we show how the RLE can be used to assess the condition of ecosystems (i) where a natural state may be impossible to achieve or undesired, and (ii) transitioning towards a different, poorly characterised state. In doing so, we underline the RLE's flexibility, which enables it to keep pace with recent conceptual and technological developments in biodiversity monitoring and ecosystem science. Practical implication: As the adoption of an ecosystem perspective in environmental management gains traction, continuing to use a common assessment framework is key for identifying critical knowledge gaps, coordinating action and sharing learnings. We call for scientists, practitioners and policy-makers to rally behind the RLE as a central framework for assessing all ecosystems, both nationally and internationally. The alternative—a proliferation of ecosystem assessment approaches—risks reducing the uptake of an ecosystem-based perspective to the management of natural resources, which would ultimately hinder our collective ability to secure ecosystem services into the future.
